meta.index.title: Evertone — a tone always at hand
meta.index.description: Evertone puts twelve pads on your Apple Watch. Tap one and the note sounds right away: for tuning, giving a choir its pitch, or finding a note to sing.
meta.privacy.title: Privacy — Evertone
meta.privacy.description: Evertone’s privacy policy: the app collects no data.
meta.support.title: Support — Evertone
meta.support.description: How to use Evertone on Apple Watch, and how to get in touch.
hero.title: A tone always at hand
hero.lead: Twelve pads on your wrist. Tap one and the note sounds right away, with no phone, no tuning fork and no piano to look for.
hero.requirements: Apple Watch with watchOS 11 or later
watch.caption: Tap a pad to listen. Tap the instrument name to change the sound.
why.title: The note, the moment you need it
why.lead: Your phone is in your bag, the tuning fork has gone missing and there’s no piano nearby. Your watch is always on your wrist. Evertone turns it into a clean tone, ready in a second.
why.tuning.title: Tuning
why.tuning.text: Guitar, violin, ukulele: play an A and tune by ear. Equal temperament, A = 440 Hz, or whatever pitch your ensemble tunes to.
why.choir.title: A pitch for the choir
why.choir.text: Give the starting note before a rehearsal or a performance, in one move, without reaching into a pocket.
why.sing.title: A note to sing
why.sing.text: Train your ear, warm up your voice, or check how an interval sounds. Every note across six octaves is under your finger.
ear.title: {app.atTheEar}: a note just for you
ear.lead: Sometimes nobody else should hear the note: in a choir before your entry, on stage, in a hall. {app.atTheEar} plays it only once the watch is at your ear, for you alone.
ear.step1.title: Hold a pad
ear.step1.text: A long press sets the note aside for later. Its pad pulses while it waits.
ear.step2.title: Raise the watch to your ear
ear.step2.text: Nothing plays until the watch is in place.
ear.step3.title: Double tap your fingers
ear.step3.text: The double tap gesture plays the note right at your ear. Tap again to repeat it.
ear.fallback: On watches without the double tap gesture, Evertone learns how you raise your hand to your ear and plays when it recognises the move.
features.title: What it does
features.instruments.title: Four instruments
features.instruments.text: {app.piano}, {app.strings}, {app.brass} and {app.voice}. Tap the name next to the clock to switch.
features.octaves.title: Six octaves
features.octaves.text: Swipe sideways, one octave at a time. Pull up to return to the last note.
features.pads.title: Twelve pads per octave
features.pads.text: Every semitone at once, large and easy to hit.
features.pitch.title: Tuning from 415 to 466 Hz
features.pitch.text: A = 440 Hz by default. For an orchestra, early music or a band that tunes differently, set A with the crown, 1 Hz at a time, and hear it right away.
features.crown.title: Volume on the crown
features.crown.text: The Digital Crown sets the volume, finely at quiet levels. Your watch remembers it.
features.instant.title: Plays instantly
features.instant.text: Sound synthesised on the watch, with no delay and no internet.
features.everyone.title: For everyone
features.everyone.text: VoiceOver, larger text, increased contrast, reduced motion and differentiate without colour. Seventeen languages.
promise.title: Collects no data
promise.text: No account, no ads, no analytics. Evertone never connects to the internet, and your settings stay on your watch.
privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: Evertone collects no data. The app has no accounts, ads or analytics, contains no third-party libraries and never connects to the internet. Nothing you do in the app reaches the developer or anyone else.
privacy.stays.title: What stays on your watch
privacy.stays.intro: To remember your choices, the app saves a few settings on the watch:
privacy.stays.item1: the instrument, volume and tuning you picked,
privacy.stays.item2: whether the {app.atTheEar} explanation has been shown,
privacy.stays.item3: on watches without the double tap gesture: how you raise your hand to your ear, a few numbers describing how the watch sits at your ear.
privacy.stays.outro: These settings live only in the watch’s storage and are removed when you delete the app. The app never sends them anywhere.
privacy.motion.title: Motion sensors
privacy.motion.text: On watches without the double tap gesture, {app.atTheEar} uses the motion sensors to tell when the watch is at your ear. Readings are analysed on the watch as they come in, only while a note is waiting to play or calibration is running. They are neither stored nor sent anywhere.
privacy.site.title: This website
privacy.site.text: This site uses no cookies, no analytics and no external fonts or scripts. Your browser keeps only the theme and language you pick. The site is hosted on GitHub Pages, whose servers, like any web server, may technically log your IP address and the time of your visit.
privacy.changes.title: Changes
privacy.changes.text: If this policy changes, the new version will appear on this page with a new date.

support.title: Support
support.requirements: Evertone runs on Apple Watch with watchOS 11 or later.
support.play.q: How do I play a note?
support.play.a: Tap a pad. The screen shows one octave, twelve semitones in three columns: from C at the top of the first column to B at the bottom of the last.
support.octave.q: How do I change the octave?
support.octave.a: Swipe sideways. A quick flick moves a whole octave; a slow drag stops at any column. Pulling up from the bottom of the screen returns to the last note you played, or to octave 5 if you haven’t played one yet.
support.instrument.q: How do I change the instrument?
support.instrument.a: Tap the instrument name next to the clock and choose {app.piano}, {app.strings}, {app.brass} or {app.voice}.
support.volume.q: How do I set the volume?
support.volume.a: Turn the Digital Crown. The volume is kept until the next launch.
support.ear.a: Hold a pad until it pulses. Raise the watch to your ear and double tap the fingers of the hand wearing it. The note plays at your ear. Tapping the pulsing pad plays it too; holding it or tapping anywhere else cancels.
support.ear.a2: Double tap is available on Apple Watch Series 9, Ultra 2 and later. On older watches, Evertone first learns the move: “{app.handOnShoulder}”, three times, with your hand on the opposite shoulder. After that it plays when it recognises the move.
support.silent.a: Turn up the volume with the crown: at its lowest setting the sound is barely audible. Also check the system volume in the watch’s Settings (Sounds & Haptics). If Bluetooth headphones are connected to the watch, the sound may be playing there.
support.tuning.a: Equal temperament with A5 = 440 Hz by default. Octave 5 is the one starting at middle C. To change the pitch, tap the instrument name next to the clock, choose {app.tuning} at the bottom of the list and turn the crown: from 415 to 466 Hz, 1 Hz at a time. After each change you hear the new A. When the pitch isn’t 440 Hz, the instrument’s icon and the frequency show next to the clock instead of its name.
support.contact.text: Something not working, or an idea? Write to
support.contact.hint: Include your watch model and watchOS version; it helps find the cause sooner.
